history: Qingdao was established in 1891; the German era left red roofs, green trees and European buildings — a 'World Architecture Expo'. The plane trees of Badaguan, seagulls at the Pier and the Taoist wonderland of Mt. Lao set the tone: red roofs, green trees, blue sea, blue sky. Tsingtao Beer was born here in 1903 and went worldwide. Today it is a city of marine science and sailing.
importance: Separately-planned city · City of brands · Sailing capital
foods: German-style brew from 1903 — beer sold in plastic bags is the city's odd sight.
Clams, conch and prawns in one pot — perfect with beer.
Plump Hongdao clams — 'swig beer, eat gala clams'.
Spanish mackerel dumplings — Qingdao's No.1 welcome dish.
Whole squid on an iron plate with sweet-spicy glaze.
Giant handmade steamed buns under Mt. Lao, full of wheat aroma.
Seaweed jelly with vinegar and garlic — a summer cooler.
Wanhechun pork-rib casserole rice — the king of Qingdao fast food.
scenes: A century-old pier promenade with seagulls — the city's card.
'World Architecture Expo' — the Granite Mansion and Princess House.
First famous mountain by the sea — the Taoist Taiqing Palace.
The red 'May Wind' sculpture and Fushan Bay nights.
The century-old brewery site — fresh beer on tap.
White lighthouse on Xiaoqingdao — 'the floating lamp'.
Gothic twin-towered church — a Zhejiang Road landmark of 100 years.
Asia's finest beach of fine sand and blue waves.
